blocks.x: Demand sensing on a governed signals spine, forecast error down 23% and finished-goods inventory down 18% at stable service levels

A consumer goods manufacturer: Plants feel data gaps in scrap rates and unplanned downtime, both traceable to decisions made hours earlier. The Achala program started at the line —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.
The baseline quarter measured the meeting: 27% weighted forecast error, 61 days of finished-goods inventory, and promotional uplifts guessed from last year's shapes rather than current signals.
Retail POS, shipment and promotional data lived in three owners' hands. The consensus number absorbed disagreement without resolving it, and supply planned to fiction with confidence.

We rebuilt sensing on a signals spine: POS, shipment, promo-calendar and external signals landed in one governed model with lineage per input, statistical sensing produced the base forecast with error measured weekly, and the consensus meeting became a short exception review, humans override with logged reasons, and the overrides themselves are scored. Supply plans to a number with a measured error bar.
